title: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" when using st.cache_data in thread
body: ### Summary If fetching data from multiple sources, it can be tempting to run code concurrently as well as cache the results. However, this causes problems when using st.experimental_memo. It results in the error: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" ### Steps to reproduce [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5402) The following code should show it quite clearly: ```python import logging import time import threading import streamlit as st from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import add_script_run_ctx [USER].experimental_memo(ttl=1) def function1(interval): interval = interval/4 logging.info("sleeping for %s seconds", interval) time.sleep(interval) logging.info("done sleeping for %s seconds", interval) return interval def main(): format = "%(asctime)s: %(message)s" logging.basicConfig(format=format) threads = [] for index in range(25): x = threading.Thread(target=function1, args=(index,)) # Hack to remove the following logging messages: # `Thread 'Thread-123': missing ScriptRunContext` # see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1326 add_script_run_ctx(x) threads.append(x) x.start() logging.info("Waiting for threads to finish") for thread in threads: thread.join() logging.info("done") st.write("done") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` **Expected behavior:** The threaded function should be run. No error should be shown. **Actual behavior:** The function runs fine. The data is cached. But, the frontend fails with an ugly error message: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" ### Is this a regression? I don't think so ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.12.2 - Python version: 3.9.13 - Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Poetry - OS version: Mac OSx 12.2.1 - Browser version: Chrome 104.0.5112.101 ### Additional information This appears to be caused by st.experimental_memo defaulting to showing a spinner while it's running. If you change line 8 to: `[USER].experimental_memo(ttl=1, show_spinner=False)` the error does not happen.
